summary: Defines four new job description attributes for IPP that let clients monitor the progress of a print job. They are optional extensions to IPP/1.0 and IPP/1.1. It updates RFC 2910 and was replaced by RFC 8011.

plainLanguage.summary: You like knowing how far along a print job is. This adds a few gauges to the printing protocol so programs can show you the progress.

questions: how to monitor ipp print job progress
what are ipp job progress attributes
subtitle: Job attributes for monitoring print job progress in IPP printers.

tldr.problem: Internet Printing Protocol (IPP) clients need a way to monitor the progress of print jobs as they are being processed, such as how many pages have been printed or which document is currently being output.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3381 adds four new job description attributes to IPP: job-collation-type identifies how sheets are ordered, sheet-completed-copy-number tracks which copy is being printed, sheet-completed-document-number identifies the current document, and impressions-completed-current-copy counts the output in the current copy. The sheet-collate job template attribute also controls how sheets are ordered within each copy.
tldr.outcome: IPP clients can now query printers to display real-time progress information to users. These attributes are optional for both clients and printers to support.

today: RFC 3381 was updated by RFC 8011, which consolidated IPP extensions and clarified the job progress attributes. The four job progress attributes are now part of the core IPP specification and are widely implemented in modern printers, enabling real-time progress reporting to users.

sections.title: Problem and Solution
sections.content:
The Internet Printing Protocol (IPP) allows computers to send print jobs to networked printers. However, IPP/1.0 and IPP/1.1 do not provide a good way for clients to monitor the progress of a job once it has been submitted. Clients cannot tell how many pages have been printed, which document is being processed in a multi-document job, or how many of the requested copies have been completed. This lack of feedback makes it difficult for users to know if a job is proceeding normally or is stuck.

RFC 3381 adds five new attributes: four job description attributes for monitoring job progress and one job template attribute for controlling sheet collation. The job description attributes provide detailed progress information at different levels of granularity. The attributes are drawn from the PWG Job Monitoring MIB and are registered as optional extensions to IPP/1.0 and IPP/1.1.
sections.plainLanguage: When you send a print job to a printer, you want to know how far it has gotten. This RFC adds four new pieces of information the printer can report: which copy is printing, which document, how many pages are done in the current copy, and how the sheets are being collated.

sections.title: Sheet Collation Control
sections.content:
The sheet-collate job template attribute controls how the printer orders media sheets when printing multiple copies of a document. This attribute affects how the progress attributes should be interpreted.

The attribute has two standard keyword values: collated and uncollated. In collated mode, the printer produces complete sets of the document in order—for example, when printing six copies of a two-page document, it prints pages 1 and 2, then pages 1 and 2 again, six times total. In uncollated mode, the printer outputs all copies of page 1, then all copies of page 2. The sheet-collate attribute works together with the multiple-document-handling attribute, which controls the ordering of multiple documents within a job. A printer indicates what it supports using the sheet-collate-supported attribute.
sections.plainLanguage: When printing multiple copies, collated means each complete copy comes out in order. Uncollated means all copies of page 1 come out first, then all copies of page 2. This matters for understanding how the progress numbers work.

sections.title: Job Progress Attributes
sections.content:
The job-collation-type enumeration describes the actual collation order the printer is using. It has five standard values: other (unknown type), unknown (the type is not reportable), uncollated-sheets (copies of each sheet are produced before moving to the next sheet), collated-documents (complete document copies are produced in order, with the i'th copy of each document before the j'th copy), and uncollated-documents (all copies of each document are produced before moving to the next document).

The sheet-completed-copy-number attribute is an integer starting at 0, set to 1 when the first sheet of the first copy begins printing, and incremented for each new copy. The sheet-completed-document-number identifies which document in a multi-document job is currently being processed. The impressions-completed-current-copy attribute counts the number of impressions (marks) made for the current copy of the current document. Each of these resets when moving to a new document or copy.
sections.plainLanguage: These four attributes tell you: how the sheets are ordered, which copy number is printing, which document is printing (in multi-document jobs), and how many pages have been done in the current copy.

sections.title: Progress Tracking Example
sections.content: Consider a three-document job with two pages per document, requesting three copies, with uncollated-sheets collation. The printer would proceed as follows: produce page 1 (impressions-completed-current-copy=1, sheet-completed-copy-number=1, sheet-completed-document-number=1), then page 2 (impressions-completed-current-copy=2), then page 1 again for the second copy (impressions-completed-current-copy=1, sheet-completed-copy-number=2), and so on. After all three copies of document 1 are complete, the attributes reset for document 2: impressions-completed-current-copy returns to 0, sheet-completed-document-number becomes 2, and sheet-completed-copy-number resets to 0. A monitoring application can use these attributes to display a progress bar showing how far along the job is, perhaps indicating "Document 2 of 3, Copy 2 of 3, Page 1 of 2."
sections.plainLanguage: As the printer works, these numbers change to show which document and copy is printing and how many pages are done. A program watching these numbers can show the user a progress bar.

sections.title: Conformance and Registration
sections.content:
All five attributes defined in RFC 3381 are optional for both IPP clients and printers to support. A printer or client is not required to implement any of them. However, if a printer advertises support for these attributes (via the sheet-collate-supported and other corresponding attributes), it MUST report the attributes accurately as documents are processed. Conformance to the RFC requires proper handling of these optional attributes only if they are implemented.

RFC 3381 registers the attributes with IANA for use in the IPP registry. Keyword values for sheet-collate include 'uncollated' and 'collated'. Enumeration values for job-collation-type include the five standard types listed in the previous section. Additional modem types and other values may be registered in the future following RFC procedures.
sections.plainLanguage: These attributes are optional, so not every printer has to support them. But if a printer says it does support them, it must report the numbers correctly as the job prints.
